2607.09328.title: WILDTRACE: Benchmarking Natural Evidence Trails in Long-Context Reasoning
2607.09328.paper_summary: Answering complex questions over long documents frequently requires integrating evidence that the source itself disperses naturally across distant passages. In an incident report, the operating condition, design flaw, and missed safety check that jointly explain a disaster may appear dozens of sections apart; in a novel, a character's true motive may surface only through scenes far removed from the moment it becomes relevant. This source-internal evidence integration is central to real-world long-document analysis, yet existing benchmarks largely sidestep it. Needle probes, planted facts, and reverse-engineered multi-hop chains embed evidence that may differ from the host text in distribution, placement, or register, making it unclear whether strong performance reflects genuine source reasoning or distributional artifacts. We introduce WILDTRACE, a benchmark of 481 tasks over 214 naturally occurring long-form sources such as technical incident reports and lesser-known literary narratives, where all evidence trails arise from the document's own causal, temporal, and narrative logic. Drawing on Pearl's causal hierarchy and prior multi-hop reasoning typologies, we define seven source-internal evidence geometries that characterize the distinct relational demands of analytical reading in long documents. A source-first construction pipeline mines candidate trails from document structure before writing questions; each item then undergoes multi-stage validation covering clue necessity, answer groundedness, rubric fidelity, contamination resistance and answerability. As models are increasingly entrusted with real-world high-stakes analytical tasks, this gap between accessing information and reasoning over naturally dispersed evidence emerges as a defining challenge for the next stage of long-context research.
2607.09328.paper_summary_zh: 回答長文件中複雜問題通常需要整合證據，而這些證據在來源本身自然分散於遙遠的段落中。在事故報告中，解釋災難的操作條件、設計缺陷和未檢查的安全措施可能相隔數十個部分；在小說中，角色的真正動機可能僅通過與其相關的場景相距甚遠的情節顯現出來。這種來源內部證據整合對於現實世界的長文件分析至關重要，但現有的基準大多避而不談。針對性探針、植入事實和逆向工程的多跳鏈條嵌入的證據在分佈、位置或語域上可能與宿主文本不同，這使得強勁的表現是否反映真實的來源推理或分佈性工件變得不明朗。我們介紹了WILDTRACE，一個涵蓋481個任務的基準，基於214個自然發生的長篇來源，如技術事故報告和較不知名的文學敘事，其中所有證據線索均源自文檔自身的因果、時間和敘事邏輯。根據Pearl的因果層級和先前的多跳推理類型，我們定義了七種來源內部證據幾何，這些幾何特徵化了長文件分析閱讀的不同關係需求。一個以來源為首的構建管道從文檔結構中挖掘候選線索，然後再撰寫問題；每個項目隨後經歷多階段驗證，涵蓋線索必要性、答案基礎、評分準則忠實度、污染抵抗力和可回答性。隨著模型越來越多地被賦予現實世界的高風險分析任務，訪問信息與對自然分散證據進行推理之間的這一差距成為長期上下文研究下一階段的定義性挑戰。
